card_says: A government corporation attached to the Department of Agriculture that builds and runs the Philippines' national irrigation systems.
source_says: NIA's own 2024 annual report says Executive Order 168 of 2022 attached it to the Department of Agriculture and Executive Order 69 of 2024 transferred it back to the Office of the President, where it sat at the time of that report; the attachment on the card holds for 2022-2024 but not after mid-2024.

company: Bukhara Regional Production State Enterprise Suvokova
card_says: Named as 'Bukhara Regional Production State Enterprise Suvokova'.
source_says: World Bank project papers of 2020 name the implementing agency as 'Bukhara Regional Production Enterprise Suvokova', without the word 'State', and say sector reform created 14 regional unitary enterprise Suvokovas. A 2019 presidential decree turned the state unitary water supply enterprises into limited liability companies and created the joint-stock company Uzsuvtaminot from them; by 2025 the Bukhara region water and sewerage works were being procured by the joint-stock company Bukhara Suv Ta'minoti under Uzsuvtaminot.

source.title: Disclosable Restructuring Paper, Uzbekistan Bukhara and Samarkand Sewerage Project (P112719)

card_says: Ukraine's state road agency, as the body responsible for the road.
source_says: The successor body's own site says the State Agency for Restoration and Infrastructure Development of Ukraine was established in January 2023 'on the foundation of Ukravtodor and Ukrinfraproekt', so Ukravtodor was the responsible body at the time of the case but has since been absorbed into that agency.

source.title: About the Agency
source.publisher: State Agency for Restoration and Infrastructure Development of Ukraine

company: Projects Implementation Unit for Water Infrastructure, Ministry of Agriculture and Water Resources of Uzbekistan
card_says: The unit sits under the Ministry of Agriculture and Water Resources of Uzbekistan.
source_says: That ministry was split in February 2018 into a Ministry of Agriculture and a Ministry of Water Resources, and World Bank reporting from 2021 places the project implementation unit under the Ministry of Water; the ministry named on the card existed when the case was written but not afterwards.

source.title: Uzbek agriculture and water resources ministry split into two

company: Ministry of Environment and Spatial Planning of Kosovo (MESP)
card_says: Named as the Ministry of Environment and Spatial Planning of Kosovo.
source_says: Kosovo's 2021 state of the environment report refers to the ministry as the Ministry of Environment, Spatial Planning and Infrastructure (MESPI), and mentions the Ministry of Environment and Spatial Planning only in the context of institutions re-established after 2000; the report gives no date for the change of name.

source.title: Report on the State of the Environment 2021

card_says: Named as rePlan Inc., as the firm that worked on the resettlement.
source_says: Trade press reported on 11 August 2015 that the environmental consultancy ERM had acquired the Toronto-based social impact and risk firm rePlan, so the firm no longer trades independently.

source.title: ERM acquires Canadian social impact and risk specialist

card_says: The card names Manila Water as the east zone concessionaire and does not state its ownership.
source_says: Manila Water's own business profile gives Trident Water as controlling shareholder with 52.16 per cent, with Philwater Holdings at 19.01 per cent and Ayala Corporation at 12.26 per cent; the Ayala group, which led the company at the time of the case documents, is now a minority holder.
